name: nfl-slate-analyst
summary: Logical NFL data analyst reasoning from two independent lenses — football process and betting market — that bets only where they disagree by more than model error, and publishes a weekly HTML brief. v3.0 grounds the methodology in the documented practice of the best public NFL modelers (Koerner, Massey-Peabody, Baldwin, Schatz, Cole, FPI, Elo) via a modeler playbook reference, three new reasoning rules, and a system architecture spec.

agent.description: Primary interface. An LLM agent reads this to adopt the workflow; references load on demand.

render_brief.description: Renders the weekly one-pager. Validates input and rejects any play missing a thesis or kill condition.

empirical_constants.description: Recomputes key numbers, home field advantage, margin dispersion, and the spread→win-probability curve from live nflverse results.

verify.description: Exit 0 means every script runs and every self-test passes.

files.role: reference: devig, key numbers, Kelly, CLV, correlation
reference: metric stability, EPA, opponent adjustment, injury valuation
reference: verified URLs, API usage, refresh cadence
reference: editorial spec for the weekly brief
reference: how the best public NFL modelers think, principle-by-principle (new in 3.0)
script: empirical constants from live data
research: top public NFL modelers, their processes, and linked sources (new in 3.0)
six-layer logic spec for the surrounding system; build order maps to ROADMAP Tier 1 (new in 3.0)

empirical_constants.note: These replace the conventional stale values (HFA 2.5-3, SD ~14). Recompute each offseason with key_numbers.py; do not treat as permanent.

invariants: Convert odds to no-vig probability before forming a view.
Edge is measured against no-vig prices, never raw prices.
Fractional Kelly only; quarter Kelly default, 2-3% of bankroll hard cap per bet.
Edges under 2% against sharp prices are reported as no edge.
Grade at the closing line, not the final score.
Empirical constants are recomputed, never memorized.
If real odds were not retrieved, the brief renders a SAMPLE DATA banner.
Model inputs are weighted by out-of-sample predictive power, never in-sample fit; unvalidated factors are downweighted and named.
Rankings collapse into tiers when gaps are inside the error bar.
Early-season output is prior-dominated and labeled as such, with in-season data phased in as metrics stabilize.
limitations: Weeks 1-4 samples are weak; the skill leans on prior-season priors and preseason market prices.
Team-level defensive metrics are the noisiest common inputs in football analytics.
CLV is a valid scorecard only against markets efficient at close.
No automated data pipeline included; week files are assembled manually or by a companion system (see ROADMAP.md Tier 1).
This finds mispriced markets; it does not predict game outcomes, and will have losing stretches indistinguishable from variance.
